title: How Gemini is speaking the language of Southeast Asia
summary: Gemini is taking off across Southeast Asia, thanks to its local language fluency and the region’s mobile-first population.
body_text: How Gemini is speaking the language of Southeast Asia Jul 14, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Active users on the Gemini app in Southeast Asia have more than doubled in the last year. Here is a look at how the region is using the chatbot in their daily life. Sapna Chadha Vice President, Southeast Asia & South Asia Frontier Samuele Saini Director, Google Ads Solutions & Insights, Southeast Asia Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Your browser does not support the audio element. Listen to article [[duration]] minutes This content is generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental Southeast Asians are adopting Gemini at record speeds, with users increasingly relying on native languages and mobile tools to work, study, and create. To build on this momentum, we are rolling out Gemini Spark in local languages to Gemini Advanced subscribers this week. This new feature acts as a proactive partner that manages tasks across your apps, even when your devices are locked. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. "How Gemini is speaking the language of Southeast Asia" explores rapid AI adoption in the region. Southeast Asians are adopting Gemini faster than any other Google app. Most users prefer interacting with Gemini in their native languages rather than English. People use Gemini on mobile devices for creative tasks, research and daily productivity. New AI agents will soon help users manage tasks across their favorite Google apps. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. People in Southeast Asia are using Gemini faster than any other Google app. Young people there love it because it understands their local languages and helps them create music, art and schoolwork. Most users talk to Gemini on their phones instead of typing. Soon, a new feature called Gemini Spark will even help them finish tasks automatically. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Explore other styles: People are making Gemini a part of their daily lives, especially in Southeast Asia. According to our first-ever Gemini Southeast Asia Report , Southeast Asians are adopting Gemini at a record-breaking pace — faster than they’ve adopted any other Google app. The number of active users on the Gemini app in the region has more than doubled in the region in a year. This growth is driven by a young, tech-savvy population (nearly 40% of the region is under 25) and Gemini’s strong performance in local languages. We dove deeper into how people are using the Gemini app across six of the region’s largest user bases: Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. The data is clear. As the Gemini app takes off across Southeast Asia, it’s becoming an indispensable companion that’s shaping how we work, study and live today. Here are some key insights about the Gemini app’s adoption in the region: Young power users: Younger digital natives are leading Gemini app adoption in Southeast Asia. They make more requests, engage in longer conversations with Gemini and write significantly more detailed prompts than other age groups. Local language fluency: Gemini’s success in the region comes down to local fluency. Nearly 70% of prompts in the region are submitted in native languages, led by Vietnam (89%), Thailand (87%) and Indonesia (84%). And according to the Southeast Asia Holistic Evaluation of Language Models (SEA-HELM) , Gemini is the overall best-performing large language model (LLM) for Southeast Asian languages. Multimodal and on-the-go: In Southeast Asia, almost 3 in 4 of Gemini requests across the region come from mobile devices. And because people can interact comfortably in their native languages, they’re bypassing keyboards — relying on voice commands, photos and video uploads for more than 40% of their prompts, and voice only for 10%, using features like Gemini Live . A creative collaborator: About 40% of queries ask Gemini to generate entirely new outputs, from generating images, music, videos to writing documents. People across Southeast Asia have generated 5 billion images with Nano Banana , our image generation model, over the past year. They’ve also generated almost 1 million songs since we introduced Lyria 3 , Gemini’s music generation model, in Southeast Asia. Research and thought partnership : People frequently rely on Gemini as a research assistant to summarize dense documents and structure messy data. They also use it as a thought partner for advice, opinions, and recommendations – like birthday gift ideas, travel destinations, and step-by-step troubleshooting. We want to make Gemini the most helpful AI assistant for the 600 million people across Southeast Asia. The next step is bringing the power of AI agents to everyone, safely and securely. That includes Gemini Spark , which transforms Gemini from an assistant that answers questions into an active partner that completes real work on your behalf. Think of Spark as a 24/7 personal AI agent designed to proactively manage your tasks. Deeply integrated with Workspace tools, like Gmail , Docs and Slides , it works in the background — even when your laptop is closed or your phone is locked. Following its initial launch in English, we’re rolling out Gemini Spark in local languages to Gemini Advanced (Ultra) subscribers this week. This builds on the powerful features people in the region already love — like Nano Banana for visual creativity, Canvas for deep learning and custom Gems for personal and professional growth. This is only the beginning of the Gemini story in Southeast Asia. We’ll continue to work toward our vision of a truly universal assistant that’s personal, proactive and powerful for the people who use it. title: Elon Musk Predictions & Outcomes: 2019 to 2026
summary: Explore Elon Musk's Tesla predictions and see which came true by 2026, including FSD progress and Optimus outcomes.
body_text: In honour of Tesla earnings, here is a list of predictions and promises made by Elon Musk from 2019 to now. We've included an indicator of which were achieved, which weren't and the eventual date of the outcome, if any. View in platform here to filter by topic, sort by date etc. Coverage window: Feb 19, 2019 to 2026-05-18 — 151 public predictions by Elon Musk about Tesla, assessed as of 2026-07-16. "Result" = whether the prediction came true by its predicted deadline (No / Yes / Yes (qualified) / Partly / Unresolved / Not yet assessable). Date Topic Prediction Predicted Deadline Result Outcome Date Assessment Notes Type Venue Prediction Sources Evidence Sources 2019-02-19 Autonomy / FSD Tesla would be feature-complete on full self-driving in 2019. 2019-12-31 No Tesla did not reach feature-complete full autonomy in 2019. Tesla still describes FSD as supervised and as not making the vehicle autonomous; NHTSA records Tesla's characterization of it as SAE Level 2. Feature-complete was Musk's term; outcome judged against unsupervised autonomy, not driver-assistance feature availability. Interview ARK Invest podcast wired.com ; Tesla, Inc., Q3 2019 Earnings Call (Oct. 23, 2019) tesla.com ; nhtsa.gov 2019-02-19 Autonomy / FSD By the end of 2020, a driver would be able to fall asleep and wake up at the destination. 2020-12-31 No The capability was not available by the end of 2020 and remains inconsistent with Tesla's current requirement for an attentive driver and active supervision. This is a concrete hands-off/sleeping-capable autonomy forecast. Interview ARK Invest podcast wired.com ; Tesla, Inc., Q1 2020 Earnings Call (Apr. 29, 2020) tesla.com ; nhtsa.gov 2019-02-19 Vehicle deliveries Tesla will make around 500,000 cars in 2019. 2019-12-31 No 2019-12-31 Tesla delivered 367,500 vehicles in 2019 and produced about 365,300, well below 500,000. Musk corrected the tweet hours later, but the original prediction itself did not come true. Original tweet assessed separately from the later correction. Tweet X / Twitter x.com ; wired.com sec.gov ; theguardian.com 2019-02-20 Vehicle production rate Tesla's annualized production rate would probably be around 500,000 vehicles at the end of 2019. 2019-12-31 No 2019-12-31 Tesla produced 104,891 vehicles in Q4 2019, an annualized rate of about 419,600, below 500,000. Annualized rate is calculated as four times Tesla's reported Q4 production. Tweet correction X / Twitter wired.com ; theguardian.com sec.gov 2019-02-20 Vehicle deliveries Tesla would deliver about 400,000 vehicles in 2019. 2019-12-31 No 2019-12-31 Tesla delivered 367,500 vehicles in 2019, about 8.1% below the corrected 400,000 forecast. Corrected delivery forecast assessed separately from the original 500,000 tweet. Tweet correction X / Twitter wired.com ; theguardian.com sec.gov 2019-04-22 Autonomy / FSD Tesla would have a no-touch, human-intervention-free self-driving system by the second quarter of 2020. 2020-06-30 No Tesla did not release unsupervised, intervention-free FSD by Q2 2020; its current FSD remains supervised and SAE Level 2. Deadline taken from the Autonomy Day presentation. Public presentation Tesla Autonomy Day youtube.com ; cbsnews.com tesla.com ; nhtsa.gov 2019-04-22 Robotaxi Tesla would have one million robotaxis on the road in 2020. 2020-12-31 No Tesla had no commercial robotaxi network in 2020. Its first limited paid robotaxi rides began in Austin on June 22, 2025 with about ten vehicles and a front-seat safety monitor. A limited 2025 pilot does not satisfy a one-million-vehicle 2020 forecast. Public presentation Tesla Autonomy Day youtube.com ; techcrunch.com reuters.com ; reuters.com 2019-04-24 Tesla Insurance Tesla hoped to launch its insurance product in about one month. 2019-05-24 No 2019-08-28 Tesla Insurance launched in California in late August 2019, roughly three months after the one-month window. Deadline normalized to one month after the call. Earnings call Tesla Q1 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q1 2019 Earnings Call (Apr. 24, 2019) tesla.com 2019-04-24 Energy storage Powerwall and Powerpack deployments could grow by roughly 300% in 2019. 2019-12-31 No Tesla reported 1.65 GWh of storage deployments in 2019 versus 1.04 GWh in 2018, an increase of about 59%, not 300%. Assessed using energy-storage capacity deployed, Tesla's reported company-wide metric. Earnings call Tesla Q1 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q1 2019 Earnings Call (Apr. 24, 2019) sec.gov 2019-04-24 Battery technology event Tesla would probably hold a battery and cell investor day later in 2019 or early in 2020. 2020-03-31 No 2020-09-22 Tesla's Battery Day was held on September 22, 2020, after the stated window. Early 2020' normalized to the end of Q1. Earnings call Tesla Q1 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q1 2019 Earnings Call (Apr. 24, 2019) tesla.com 2019-05-09 Autonomy / FSD A Tesla would drive from Los Angeles to New York with no human intervention by the end of 2019. 2019-12-31 No No such intervention-free cross-country Tesla trip occurred by the deadline. Tesla's production FSD still requires active driver supervision. The tweet revived and generalized an earlier cross-country promise. Tweet X / Twitter x.com ; autopilotreview.com tesla.com ; nhtsa.gov 2019-07-24 Gigafactory Shanghai Gigafactory Shanghai would be producing Model 3s in volume by the end of 2019. 2019-12-31 Yes 2019-12-31 Tesla reported that Shanghai had begun trial production in Q4 2019 and had demonstrated a production run-rate above 3,000 vehicles per week before year-end. Earnings call Tesla Q2 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q2 2019 Earnings Call (Jul. 24, 2019) ir.tesla.com ; sec.gov 2019-07-24 Profitability Tesla expected to be around breakeven in Q3 2019 and profitable in Q4 2019. 2019-12-31 Yes 2019-12-31 Tesla reported positive GAAP net income attributable to common stockholders in both Q3 and Q4 2019, satisfying the breakeven/profitability forecast. Earnings call Tesla Q2 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q2 2019 Earnings Call (Jul. 24, 2019) ir.tesla.com ; ir.tesla.com 2019-07-24 Gigafactory location Tesla would finalize and announce its European Gigafactory location before the end of 2019. 2019-12-31 Yes 2019-11-12 Musk announced Berlin as the European Gigafactory location on November 12, 2019. Earnings call Tesla Q2 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q2 2019 Earnings Call (Jul. 24, 2019) reuters.com ; tesla.com 2019-07-24 Battery technology event Tesla's battery technology event would probably take place in February or March 2020. 2020-03-31 No 2020-09-22 Tesla held Battery Day on September 22, 2020, about six months after the stated window. A more specific revision of the Q1 2019 event forecast; retained because the deadline changed. Earnings call Tesla Q2 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q2 2019 Earnings Call (Jul. 24, 2019) tesla.com 2019-07-24 Gigafactory Berlin Tesla would probably have an operational European Gigafactory in 2021. 2021-12-31 No 2022-03-22 Tesla opened Gigafactory Berlin-Brandenburg and delivered the first vehicles in March 2022, after 2021. Earnings call Tesla Q2 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q2 2019 Earnings Call (Jul. 24, 2019) bbc.com ; tesla.com 2019-10-23 Model Y Model Y production would begin by summer 2020. 2020-09-22 Yes 2020-01-29 Tesla reported that Model Y production began in January 2020 and deliveries started in March, several months before summer. Summer deadline normalized to the September equinox; production actually began much earlier. Earnings call Tesla Q3 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q3 2019 Earnings Call (Oct. 23, 2019); businessinsider.com ir.tesla.com ; ir.tesla.com 2019-10-23 Model Y Tesla expected Model Y volume production above 1,000 vehicles per week no later than mid-2020. 2020-06-30 Unresolved Tesla began Model Y production and deliveries in early 2020, but its public Q2 reporting combined Model 3 and Model Y output, so the specific 1,000-per-week threshold by June cannot be independently verified. Kept separate from the existing Model Y start-date forecast because this forecast specified a volume threshold. Earnings call Tesla Q3 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q3 2019 Earnings Call (Oct. 23, 2019) ir.tesla.com ; sec.gov 2019-11-21 Cybertruck Cybertruck production would start in late 2021. 2021-12-31 No 2023-11-30 Customer deliveries began at a November 30, 2023 delivery event, roughly two years late. Late fulfillment is recorded as No because the requested test is within the predicted timeline. Product unveiling Cybertruck reveal theverge.com ; Tesla, Inc., Q3 2020 Earnings Call (Oct. 21, 2020); Tesla, Inc., Q4 2020 Earnings Call (Jan. 27, 2021) tesla.com ; wired.com 2019-11-21 Cybertruck The base Cybertruck would start at $39,900. 2023-11-30 No 2023-11-30 At the 2023 delivery event Tesla priced the least-expensive announced version at $60,990; the later offered Long Range version was also far above $39,900. Nominal prices; tax credits and incentives excluded. Product unveiling Cybertruck reveal greencarreports.com ; theverge.com wired.com ; reuters.com 2019-11-21 Cybertruck The tri-motor Cybertruck would have more than 500 miles of range. 2023-11-30 No 2023-11-30 Production Cybertruck versions announced at delivery had about 320 to 340 miles of estimated range, not 500-plus miles. Range-extender concepts that were not delivered are not counted. Product unveiling Cybertruck reveal greencarreports.com ; theverge.com wired.com ; tesla.com 2020-01-29 Vehicle deliveries Tesla should comfortably exceed 500,000 vehicle deliveries in 2020. 2020-12-31 No 2020-12-31 Tesla delivered 499,550 vehicles in 2020, 450 short of 500,000; therefore it did not literally exceed 500,000, let alone comfortably. Strict threshold assessment; the miss was only about 0.09%. Earnings call Tesla Q4 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q4 2019 Earnings Call (Jan. 29, 2020); fool.com ir.tesla.com 2020-01-29 Autonomy / FSD Tesla would be feature-complete on Full Self-Driving in a couple of months. 2020-03-31 No Tesla did not deliver unsupervised feature-complete driving by March 2020; Tesla still describes FSD as supervised and not autonomous. A couple of months' normalized to March 31, 2020. This is a revised deadline, not a duplicate of the 2019 deadline. Earnings call Tesla Q4 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q4 2019 Earnings Call (Jan. 29, 2020) tesla.com ; nhtsa.gov 2020-01-29 Battery technology event Tesla's Battery Day would probably be in April 2020. 2020-04-30 No 2020-09-22 Battery Day occurred on September 22, 2020. A later, more specific deadline revision. Earnings call Tesla Q4 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q4 2019 Earnings Call (Jan. 29, 2020) tesla.com 2020-01-29 Model S Plaid Tesla expected the Plaid powertrain and vehicle to be available by the end of 2020. 2020-12-31 No 2021-06-10 Tesla delivered the first Model S Plaid vehicles in June 2021. Earnings call Tesla Q4 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q4 2019 Earnings Call (Jan. 29, 2020) reuters.com 2020-04-12 Robotaxi Robotaxi functionality would still be ready in 2020, subject to regulatory approval. 2020-12-31 No No Tesla robotaxi functionality capable of commercial driverless service was delivered in 2020; FSD remained supervised. Regulatory approval was not the only missing condition; technical supervision remained required. Tweet X / Twitter caranddriver.com ; Tesla, Inc., Q3 2019 Earnings Call (Oct. 23, 2019) tesla.com ; nhtsa.gov 2020-04-29 FSD subscription Tesla would release an FSD subscription option by the end of 2020. 2020-12-31 No 2021-07-17 Tesla launched the monthly FSD subscription in July 2021. Earnings call Tesla Q1 2020 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q1 2020 Earnings Call (Apr. 29, 2020) theverge.com 2020-04-29 Gigafactory location Tesla would announce its next U.S. Gigafactory location within one to three months. 2020-07-29 Yes 2020-07-22 Tesla announced Austin, Texas, as the location of its next Gigafactory on July 22, 2020, within three months of the call. Deadline is three months after the call, the outer edge of the stated range. Earnings call Tesla Q1 2020 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q1 2020 Earnings Call (Apr. 29, 2020) cnbc.com 2020-04-29 Solar Roof Tesla aimed to install 1,000 Solar Roofs per week by the end of 2020. 2020-12-31 No Wood Mackenzie estimated only about 3,000 Solar Roof installations in total through early 2023, with the best quarter averaging roughly 32 systems per week, far below 1,000 per week. Earnings call Tesla Q1 2020 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q1 2020 Earnings Call (Apr. 29, 2020) woodmac.com ; sec.gov 2020-04-29 Robotaxi Tesla could deploy robotaxis in some markets in 2021, subject to regulatory approval. 2021-12-31 No 2025-06-22 Tesla did not operate a driverless commercial robotaxi service in any market in 2021; its first limited paid Austin robotaxi service began in June 2025. Earnings call Tesla Q1 2020 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q1 2020 Earnings Call (Apr. 29, 2020) reuters.com ; tesla.com 2020-07-09 Autonomy / FSD Tesla was very close to Level 5 and would have the basic functionality complete in 2020. 2020-12-31 No Tesla did not achieve Level 5 or complete its basic functionality in 2020. Current FSD remains supervised and Tesla characterizes it as SAE Level 2. Level 5 means full automation under all driving conditions. Video address World Artificial Intelligence Conference reuters.com ; Tesla, Inc., Q2 2020 Earnings Call (Jul. 22, 2020) tesla.com ; nhtsa.gov 2020-09-22 Affordable vehicle Battery advances would enable a compelling $25,000 fully autonomous Tesla in about three years. 2023-09-22 No Tesla had not launched a $25,000 car by September 2023 or by the assessment date. Even Tesla's lower-priced 2025 Model 3 and Model Y variants were roughly $36,990 and $39,990 before incentives, and FSD remained supervised. Three years measured from Battery Day. Public presentation Tesla Battery Day tesla.com ; greencarreports.com assets-ir.tesla.com ; tesla.com 2020-09-22 Battery production Tesla aimed to reach 3 terawatt-hours per year of battery-cell production by 2030. 2030-12-31 Not yet assessable The 2030 deadline has not arrived. This row records the forecast but does not score present capacity as a failure before the deadline. Aspirational production target with an explicit date; included because it is measurable. Public presentation Tesla Battery Day tesla.com ; rev.com tesla.com ; assets-ir.tesla.com 2020-09-22 Vehicle production Tesla would probably produce 20 million vehicles per year before 2030. 2029-12-31 Not yet assessable The deadline has not arrived. Tesla delivered 1.64 million vehicles in 2025, so reaching 20 million annually would require a very large later ramp, but early scoring would be inappropriate. Before 2030' normalized to December 31, 2029. Public presentation Tesla Battery Day businessinsider.com ; tesla.com assets-ir.tesla.com ; tesla.com 2020-10-12 Autonomy / FSD Tesla would release a limited FSD beta on Tuesday, October 20, 2020. 2020-10-20 Yes 2020-10-20 Tesla began the limited FSD beta release on October 20, 2020, matching the stated day. This predicts a beta release, not autonomous capability. Tweet X / Twitter engadget.com ; teslarati.com x.com ; theverge.com 2020-10-21 Gigafactory Berlin and Texas Tesla expected Gigafactory Berlin and Gigafactory Texas to produce and deliver vehicles in 2021. 2021-12-31 No 2022-04-07 Customer deliveries from both factories began in 2022: Berlin in March and Texas in April. The same forecast was repeated on the Q4 2020 call and is consolidated here. Earnings call Tesla Q3 2020 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q3 2020 Earnings Call (Oct. 21, 2020) bbc.com ; tesla.com 2020-10-21 Energy storage Tesla expected energy-storage deployments to roughly double in 2021. 2021-12-31 No Tesla's storage deployments rose from about 3.0 GWh in 2020 to 4.0 GWh in 2021, roughly 32%, not 100%. Earnings call Tesla Q3 2020 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q3 2020 Earnings Call (Oct. 21, 2020) sec.gov ; sec.gov 2021-01-27 Autonomy / FSD Tesla expected FSD reliability to exceed a human driver in 2021. 2021-12-31 No Tesla did not demonstrate or deploy unsupervised driving that exceeded human reliability in 2021. title: Rigel Appoints Board Member Alison L. Hannah, M.D. as Chief Medical Officer
body_text: Dr. Hannah has decades of oncology drug development experience and has served on Rigel's Board of Directors since 2021 She has resigned from Rigel's Board of Directors to join the company SOUTH SAN FRANCISCO, Calif. , July 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Rigel Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Nasdaq: RIGL), a commercial stage biotechnology company focused on hematologic disorders and cancer, today announced the appointment of Alison L. Hannah, M.D. to the role of Executive Vice President and Chief Medical Officer. Dr. Hannah has resigned from Rigel's Board of Directors, effective July 1, 2026, in connection with her appointment. She succeeds Lisa Rojkjaer, M.D., as Chief Medical Officer. "Alison has been a valued member of Rigel's Board, and we are pleased to welcome her to the executive leadership team as Chief Medical Officer at an exciting time for Rigel. Her deep experience leading oncology clinical development and advancing investigational therapies through the regulatory process will be extremely valuable as we continue to advance our development pipeline, including R289 in lower-risk MDS, vepdegestrant in metastatic breast cancer and other potential opportunities," said Raul Rodriguez, Rigel's president and CEO. "On behalf of the entire Rigel team, I want to sincerely thank Lisa for her dedication and many contributions to the company." Rigel's leading pipeline asset, R2891, a potent and selective dual inhibitor of interleukin receptor-associated kinases 1 and 4 (IRAK1/4), continues to be advanced in its Phase 1b clinical study evaluating the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and preliminary efficacy in patients with relapsed or refractory lower-risk myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS). Enrollment in the dose expansion phase of the study is ongoing, and Rigel remains on track to complete enrollment and select the recommended Phase 2 dose for future clinical studies in the second half of 2026. The company continues to anticipate sharing preliminary data from the dose expansion phase of the study by the end of 2026. In addition, Rigel is progressing its evaluation of other potential indications to advance R289 and is planning to provide an update later this year. "I am excited to join Rigel at this important stage in the company's evolution. Having served on Rigel's Board, I have seen firsthand the strength of the team, the scientific rationale behind its programs and the opportunity to advance meaningful new therapies for patients with hematologic disorders and cancer," said Dr. Hannah. "I look forward to working closely with the leadership team to help guide the continued development of R289 and Rigel's broader clinical strategy, including the recent addition of vepdegestrant." About Dr. Hannah Alison L. Hannah, M. D. has been appointed Executive Vice President and Chief Medical Officer (CMO) of Rigel. She resigned from Rigel's Board of Directors, which she had served on since May 2021, in connection with her appointment as CMO. Previously, Dr. Hannah has held the roles of Chief Medical Officer of CytomX Therapeutics, where she oversaw clinical development of conditionally activated protein therapeutics, and Senior Medical Director at SUGEN, Inc. (acquired by Pharmacia & Upjohn, now Pfizer), where she had oversight of clinical development, clinical operations, and pharmacovigilance, specializing in the development of tyrosine kinase inhibitors, including sunitinib (SUTENT) approved for the treatment of kidney cancer and imatinib-refractory gastrointestinal stromal tumors. Dr. Hannah has served as a consultant to the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industry since 2000, directing the development of investigational cancer therapies. In this capacity, Dr. Hannah has successfully filed over 40 regulatory applications for first-in-human clinical testing and has played significant roles in the broad marketing approval of multiple anticancer therapeutics. title: ASE Announces FOCoS-Bridge with TSV; Latest Package Technology Reduces Power Loss by 3x for Next-Generation AI and HPC Applications
summary: This innovation improves performance by increasing bandwidth, shortening delivery paths, and enabling higher I/O density and better thermal dissipation. The integration of TSV boosts ASE’s VIPack™ FOCoS-Bridge capabilities, addressing the critical need for energy efficiency in emerging AI and high-performance computing applications.
body_text: SUNNYVALE, Calif., May 28, 2025 – Advanced Semiconductor Engineering, Inc. (ASE), a member of ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. (NYSE: ASX, TAIEX: 3711), today announced Fan-Out Chip-on-Substrate-Bridge (FOCoS-Bridge) with Through Silicon Via (TSV), propelling technology enablement for artificial intelligence (AI) and its pervasive impact on global life. Delivering critical performance improvements, ASE’s FOCoS-Bridge with TSV addresses growing demand for increased bandwidth by creating a shorter delivery path through TSV and enabling a higher I/O density and enhanced thermal dissipation. The integration of TSV expands ASE’s VIPack™ FOCoS-Bridge capabilities to deliver critical energy efficiency at a time when the need has never been greater across emerging AI and high-performance computing (HPC) applications. Future chiplet and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) integration will require higher interconnection densities to accommodate parallel higher data rate links and to preserve signal integrity. High-density interconnection is a key enabler of chiplet integration. AI and HPC power delivery requirements are becoming more complex and now necessitate advanced bridge chips with TSV features. The VIPack FOCoS-Bridge platform can be utilized for embedding passives and active dies, which can help improve power integrity and provide direct access for improved performance. “Artificial intelligence is increasingly integrated across a broad spectrum of applications—from intelligent manufacturing systems and autonomous vehicles to next-generation retail infrastructure and precision medical diagnostics—driving exponential growth in computational requirements and energy efficiency demands,” said Yin Chang, Executive Vice President at ASE. “Our introduction of the FOCoS-Bridge with TSV underscores ASE’s strategic commitment to supporting the AI ecosystem with advanced heterogeneous integration solutions. This innovation enhances our VIPack portfolio, offering a scalable, high-density packaging platform optimized for sustainable, high-performance computing architectures.” The expansion of ASE’s VIPack platform reflects the company’s strategic vision to provide a comprehensive, scalable ecosystem for sustainable, high-performance computing that meets the rigorous demands of emerging AI workloads. ASE’s FOCoS-Bridge with TSV can fulfill next-generation AI and HPC performance demands through heterogenous integration for high-power and high-bandwidth systems. Progress has been demonstrated using an 85mm x 85mm test vehicle comprised of two identical fan-out modules. Each module is made up of one ASIC chip and four HBM3 chips that are laterally interconnected with four TSV bridge chips as well as 10 integrated passive device chips. The TSV bridge chips provide a new shorter vertical path for power delivery in conjunction with traditional lateral signal connections. The TSV and passive devices are embedded and interconnected using three redistribution layers (RDLs) with 5µm line and space. When compared to FOCoS-Bridge, the resistance and inductance of FOCoS-Bridge TSV are significantly reduced by 72% and 50%, respectively. “The growing demands of HPC and AI applications are accelerating the need for greater computational performance, and ASE’s FOCoS-Bridge capabilities enable seamless integration of SoCs and chiplets with high-bandwidth memory,” said Teck Lee, Director of R&D at ASE. “By incorporating TSV, FOCoS-Bridge enhances compute and energy efficiency, and elevates our advanced packaging portfolio to the next level.” FOCoS-Bridge technology has already demonstrated its ability to address higher bandwidth and faster data transfer rates in AI and HPC applications. It leverages the advantages of highly integrated fan-out structures to overcome the limitations of traditional electrical interconnects, and enables high-speed, low-latency, and energy-efficient data communication between processors, accelerators, and memory modules. While establishing the foundation for embedding passives and active chips in the fan-out package, FOCoS-Bridge also provides options of decoupling capacitor integration for power delivery optimization and active dies for interconnection between to certain functions, such as memory, I/O, and more. “ASE is strategically positioned at the forefront of the industry as a premier provider of advanced packaging solutions for high-power AI and high-performance computing applications,” said Charles Lee, Director of Engineering and Technical Promotion at ASE. “Our strength lies in our ability to deliver innovative technologies that address customers’ evolving needs in a rapidly advancing market.” ASE will participate at ECTC 2025 in Dallas, May 27-30, 2025, with an exhibition showcasing our VIPack technologies, while delivering a suite of technologist presentations and panelist opinion across the conference program. title: Stripe for Hotels: Why It Often Fails and What to Use Instead
summary: Stripe works well for e-commerce. For hotels and tour operators in emerging markets, it's a different story. Here's what actually happens — and what to use instead.
body_text: Stripe is the first place most people look when they want to start accepting card payments online. It's well-known, the documentation is good, and it works seamlessly for e-commerce businesses in the US and Europe. For a lot of hotels, tour operators, and activity providers in Asia, Africa, and Latin America, it is either not available in their country, or it doesn't well. The most common problem is account freezes. Stripe classifies tourism as high-risk, which means your account can be suspended - sometimes without warning - if you process too many refunds, receive chargebacks, or simply trigger their fraud filters. For a hotel that relies on card payments to collect deposits and confirm bookings, a frozen account is an immediate cash flow crisis. Stripe operates in around 45 countries. If you're running a property in Kenya, Bolivia, Indonesia, or most of West Africa, you can't create a Stripe account at all. If you were to use a registered business address in another country, there are complications with payouts and tax. For hotels that do get Stripe working, American Express is often the next issue. Stripe supports American Express in theory, but in practice a significant number of American Express transactions decline when processed through Stripe accounts in South America, Africa, and Asia. For properties that host a lot of US and European travellers, who disproportionately carry American Express, this means turning away payments from some of your highest-spending guests. Stripe lacks a lot of features for tourism businesses. It's built for e-commerce - recurring subscriptions, online storefronts, marketplaces. It has no way to charge the virtual credit cards that OTAs like Booking.com and Expedia send through, and no mechanism for sending a payment request over WhatsApp. These are everyday workflows for a hotel. PayPal has most of the same problems, plus fees that compound badly on international transactions. A tour operator in Vietnam paying PayPal's exchange rate markup can lose dollars per transaction before the standard fee even kicks in. The platforms that tend to work for tourism businesses in emerging markets are purpose-built for the use case. Tab, for example, supports card acceptance in markets where Stripe and PayPal don't operate, accepts American Express, doesn't freeze accounts based on tourism industry classification, and is built around the workflows that hotels and tour operators actually use - payment links, advance deposits, OTA virtual card charging, and an embeddable booking widget for direct bookings. The fee structure is also straightforward: 2.9% plus $1 for advance bookings, 2.9% for in-person payments, with free payouts to any bank account in 140+ currencies every week. No monthly fees, no setup costs, no hardware. Disclosure: Availability, onboarding requirements, and payment-workflow support vary by country, business model, and provider. Information in this article is accurate as of May 18, 2026. Sources: Stripe global availability, Stripe restricted-business guidance, Stripe’s hotel payment processing guide, Booking.com and Expedia documentation on OTA payment flows.

summary: Discover the surprising effects of Ambien beyond sleep. Learn about its unexpected side effects and make informed choices for better health and well-being.
body_text: Explore the surprising side effects of Ambien and understand how this sleep aid can paradoxically worsen insomnia and provoke other unexpected reactions. Dr. Shiyan Yeo, Internal Medicine Physician, Sleep Medicine Expert: “Ambien may impair coordination, memory, and alertness even after waking—especially if not timed properly.” Take the first step towards improving your sleep with Sleep Reset. Start by taking our sleep quiz , enabling us to pinpoint your key issues. Following the quiz, opt to work with your personal sleep coach and gain access to our dedicated sleep program. It's a proactive approach to address sleep concerns without the risks associated with medications like Ambien. Sleeping pills vs. Sleep Reset Insomnia and Sleep Disturbances Ironically, those prescribed Ambien to alleviate sleep disturbances may find themselves in a paradox. Instead of providing relief, this medication has the potential to intensify symptoms, turning peaceful night's slumbers into bouts of wakefulness and restlessness. Patients seek Ambien for its sleep-inducing properties, but sometimes it backfires, inducing a worsening spiral of insomnia. Rather than improving sleep quality, it exacerbates the very condition it was meant to mitigate, catching patients in an unforgiving cycle of disturbed sleep. The Paradoxical Effect of Ambien Ambien, known for inducing sleep in insomnia sufferers , can introduce a paradoxical effect. This counterintuitive reaction amplifies restless and agitation, the exact symptoms individuals seek to eliminate with Ambien use. Ambien may have a counterproductive effect leading to heightened restlessness and aggravated insomnia, necessitating medication adjustments. Notably, this paradoxical outcome can be particularly disruptive for patients. Instead of improving sleep patterns, it can deteriorate them, leading to longer, more severely restless nights. It's crucial to understand the potentially backfiring impact of Ambien. Unforeseen repercussions, such as increased agitation and insomnia, can necessitate changes in a patient's medication regimen. Worsening of Sleep Quality While intended as a sleep aid, Ambien paradoxically may degrade sleep quality over time. Chronic use can lead to fragmented sleep, frequent awakenings, and decreased slow-wave sleep, disrupting restorative sleep phases. Ambien's negative impact on sleep quality is significant. Rebound insomnia, a condition where sleep disturbances are worse after stopping medication, is common. This effect raises fresh questions about the efficacy of medication-assisted sleeping. Nightmares and Confusion Chilling nightmares can be a disturbing aftermath of Ambien use. These vivid, distressing dreams often disrupt sleep rather than promote it, adding a brutal irony to your quest for rest. Ambien-induced disorientation is another unnerving side effect. When users awaken at night, they often experience profound confusion, making even the most familiar environments seem strange and bewildering. Cognitive Impairment Dr. Michael Grandner, Sleep Expert, Professor of Neuroscience and Physiological Sciences: “Some people experience complex behaviors like sleep-eating or even sleep-driving. These risks should never be ignored.” Ambien's stealthy impact on cerebral performance can manifest as memory deficits and hindered decision-making. Ambien use, aside from initiating sleep, brings forth cognitive risks, subtly impairing crucial mental processes. Memory Problems Ambien, known generically as zolpidem tartrate, poses an increasing risk of memory problems , which can be disconcerting for many users. This potential side effect is often referred to as 'Ambien Amnesia,' characterizing disruptions in forming and recalling memories while under the influence of the medication. Amnesia episodes due to Ambien usually occur if users do not sleep immediately after taking the drug. Complete blackouts and inability to remember actions performed while on the medication may occur. Incorrect or reduced dosage can alleviate this side effect, while prolonged misuse may result in sustained memory impairment. Delirium or temporary periods of disorientation, delusion, or hallucinations may accompany memory problems. Impaired Judgment and Decision-Making One prominent cognitive side effect of Ambien can be impaired judgment and decision-making, leading to surprising and sometimes dangerous consequences. This consequence is particularly concerning as it can distort a patient's rationality or cognitive performance, often without their awareness. Unexpected impulsive behavior Decreased problem-solving skills Risk-taking behavior or poor risk assessment skills Difficulty in making sound judgments Impaired motor skills, potentially leading to accidents. Addiction and Dependence Ambien, intended for short-term relief from insomnia, can ironically become a source of substantial reliance. The slow, often unnoticed, slide into dependency can pivot a solution into a potential problem. Early signs of addiction range from escalating dosage without a doctor's guidance to increasing preoccupation with the drug. Unmasking these signs can be instrumental in averting the subtle, insidious creep of Ambien addiction. Tolerance and Increased Dosage The more you consume Ambien, the more your body builds a tolerance towards it. This increased tolerance often leads to a higher dosage, escalating the scale of usage, subsequently increasing potential risks. Amplified tolerance to the effects of the drugs over time. Increased dosage to achieve desired sleep results. Heightened dependence due to prolonged usage. Augmented risk of adverse side effects. Possible escalation towards misuse and addiction. Withdrawal Symptoms Facing sudden withdrawal from Ambien can trigger a cascade of ripple effects. Patients may experience rebound insomnia, anxiety, tremors, and, quite rarely, even seizures, highlighting the importance of medical supervision during dosage reduction. Being able to pinpoint symptoms of Ambien withdrawal contributes significantly to effective management. Symptoms can encompass physical discomfort, emotional unsteadiness, or sleep disturbances, with individuals often experiencing more intense insomnia than prior to medication use. Behavioral Changes Despite its intended use to facilitate sleep, Ambien can notably exhibit personality alterations and provoke unpredictable behaviors. In essence, a calm and collective person can unexpectedly become agitated and behave erratically. Aggression, irritability, and unpredictable actions are some of the veiled side effects of Ambien. In some individuals, these alterations can escalate quickly, leading to critical mental health issues that extend well beyond a disturbed night's sleep. Mood Swings and Emotional Instability Ambien can precipitate unsettling emotional upheavals, causing users to grapple with fluctuating temperaments and moods. This volatility may often leave the individual as well as those around them in a state of constant unease. Further, the drug's emotional whirl may exacerbate or usher in conditions like depression or anxiety.
